Article Title: NCBS researcher from Bengaluru wins Google PhD Fellowship
Article Text:
Surya Sarathi Das

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: A doctoral researcher at the National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) has been selected for the 2026 Google PhD Fellowship, becoming the first PhD student from the institute to receive the recognition.Surya Sarathi Das, who works in the laboratory of Sabarinathan Radhakrishnan at NCBS, has been selected in the Health Research category, representing India. The fellowship, supported by Google.org, will fund his research exploring how artificial intelligence (AI) can help assess the risk of cervical cancer recurrence using routinely available digital pathology data.Das’ doctoral research examines how the integration of human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA into the tumour genome and the expression of viral genes influence tumour behaviour and patient outcomes. A key focus is understanding why some patients experience a recurrence of cervical cancer while others do not.His team has identified a molecular marker that could help distinguish patients at higher risk of relapse. With the fellowship support, Das plans to develop and evaluate AI models that can predict this biomarker directly from digital pathological data. This could potentially make risk assessment more affordable and accessible, particularly in resource-constrained healthcare settings.“Through my PhD research, I have been trying to understand why some patients with cervical cancer experience recurrence while others do not. With the support from Google, I hope to take this work further by exploring AI-based approaches to predict this marker and assess recurrence risks,” Das said.Radhakrishnan said the research could help clinicians improve patient stratification and tailor treatment and follow-up based on individual risks, with the long-term objective of reducing recurrence.Das is among 148 researchers selected for the 2026 fellowship across 38 countries. Google.org is providing $13 million in funding for this year's cohort. The programme supports early-career researchers advancing the science of AI, offering financial assistance for doctoral research and opportunities to engage with a global network of researchers.Since its launch in 2009, the Google PhD Fellowship Programme has supported more than 1,100 graduate students worldwide.
Article Summary: Surya Sarathi Das is the first PhD student from the National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) to receive the recognition. The fellowship, supported by Google.org, will fund his research exploring how artificial intelligence (AI) can help assess the risk of cervical cancer recurrence.

Article Title: Peace through strength: Quad confronts economic coercion, unilateral actions
Article Text:
PM Modi pitched a Quad meeting in early 2027

Amid doubts not about Quad's survival but the level at which it will function, the leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the US - PM Anthony Albanese, PM Narendra Modi, PM Sanae Takaichi and President Donald Trump respectively - met in Manila Tuesday for the first summit in 2 years.They looked to turn up the heat on China as they expressed grave concerns over economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions, and committed to working together to ensure open, safe, and resilient maritime transit corridors in the Indo-Pacific.The president described Quad as very important and special - and Modi as a friend and a great leader - in his opening remarks, as he announced Quad will conduct its first exercise featuring maritime patrol aircraft, working to protect "peace through strength".However, the short joint press release – unlike the expansive 2024 Wilmington Declaration – cut Beijing some slack by not explicitly mentioning South or East China Sea even though it strongly opposed any "destabilizing or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability".Modi pitched hosting a Quad business leaders’ summit early next year.The meeting took place hours before Trump's departure for China, where he is set to attend a potentially landmark trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin. Trump said Quad nations had reached several new critical mineral deals to secure their supply chains and ensure that none of them remained vulnerable to coercion by any single foreign supplier.The joint statement that P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context "making our seas safer". The exercise will take place in Guam next year under the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration, a new initiative that was launched in May this year to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness.Importantly for India – amid growing US-Pakistan ties – the joint statement unequivocally condemned terrorism and violent extremism in all its forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism, and committed to strengthening the Quad’s ongoing cooperation on counterterrorism.Calling the meeting in Manila an important milestone, Modi said that for India, Quad is a constructive and trusted partnership. "From maritime security to trusted supply chains, new technologies to disaster response, it has been our endeavour that the Quad provides trusted solutions for the entire Indo-Pacific," he said in his opening remarks, underlining the political will behind the partnership.The statement also said that Quad is working to secure critical supply chains, protecting freedom of navigation and overflight, driving growth through technologies of the future including investments and deployment of trusted Artificial Intelligence (AI), and responding to disasters with life-saving assistance.Expectedly, AI was a major area of focus with the leaders backing AI Accelerator, which was announced by the foreign ministers on the margins of the G20 meeting in Atlanta, and is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted AI access, deployment, and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific. "We want to ensure that the future of this critical technology is dominated by nations that share our values and our common interests," said Trump.Foreign secretary Vikram Misri said that the Quad leaders agreed to launch a Quad business forum for the first time bringing together businesses, academics and industries to foster greater business ties across private sectors, including the promotion of commercial deals and partnerships critical to the prosperity of the Indo-Pacific.The joint statement recalled that this year marks nearly a decade since the Quad was revived and the tenth anniversary of the vision of a Free and Open Indo-Pacific, first articulated by the late Japanese PM Shinzo Abe in 2016. "A decade on, that vision is stronger than ever. Together, we have shown that the Quad is a force for good and a partnership of action, committed to peace, stability, and prosperity," it said.
Article Summary: The leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the US - PM Anthony Albanese, PM Narendra Modi, PM Sanae Takaichi and President Donald Trump respectively - met in Manila Tuesday for the first summit in 2 years. They expressed grave concerns over economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions, and committed to working together to ensure open, safe, and resilient maritime transit corridors.

NEW DELHI: Meta has tightened Instagram 's recommendations in India, disclosing the changes a month after the govt asked it to review how Instagram and Facebook suggest posts. Meta said Instagram now recommends fewer sexually suggestive posts and depictions of violence.The changes apply to suggested posts from accounts users do not follow, including in Reels, and the main feed. Posts complying with Instagram's rules can remain on the platform even if they are excluded from recommendations.Meta said it had strengthened its default safeguards over the past year based on user feedback. Instagram uses AI models to assess posts before recommending them and has fine-tuned its systems for India to identify more sensitive material."We've seen people report recommended content about half as often as they were a year ago," Meta said in a blog post. The company did not disclose the underlying figures.In its Oct 10 advisory, the IT ministry asked Meta to review how it ranks and recommends posts, citing concerns that its systems could give undue prominence to misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material. It also sought stronger checks on posts that could incite violence or disrupt public order.The IT ministry asked Meta to ensure that users were not disproportionately exposed to a narrow set of narratives and to report back on the steps it had taken. Meta did not link the Instagram changes to the advisory or say whether it had changed how either platform recommends posts about events in India.
Article Summary: The changes apply to suggested posts from accounts users do not follow, including in Reels, and the main feed. The IT ministry asked Meta to review how it ranks and recommends posts, citing concerns that its systems could give undue prominence to misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material.

Article Title: Multiple NEET attempts, weightage to class 12 scores: States' suggestions to Nilekani panel
Article Text:
States have suggested multiple NEET-UG attempts in a year and weightage to Class 12 scores as part of examination reforms being examined by the Nilekani-led panel

Task force gets more time to submit report

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Several states have suggested allowing students to take the NEET-UG medical entrance examination more than once a year and giving Class 12 board examination scores some weightage in admissions. The proposals have been made to a high-powered task force led by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani , which is examining reforms to national-level examinations, news agency PTI reported citing sources.The suggestions aim to reduce students' dependence on a single high-stakes entrance test. The six-member panel has received more than 50,000 submissions from students, parents, teachers, academic institutions, experts and other stakeholders."Certain states have proposed that NEET-UG should be conducted more than once a year to reduce the pressure of a single high-stakes examination. There are also recommendations that Class 12 should be given some weightage," PTI quoted a source as saying."The panel is yet to meet representatives from all states and seek their recommendations," the source added.The Centre has extended the task force's tenure till January 2027.It was initially expected to submit its report by October 2026, but the government granted it additional time as consultations with stakeholders are still underway.The panel is examining ways to make national-level examinations more secure and prevent question paper leaks through the use of technology.Among the proposals being considered are a secure question vault, a large pool of questions prepared and verified throughout the year, and digital delivery of question papers to examination centres shortly before tests begin.The task force was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on July 26, 2026, a day after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union education minister following widespread protests over examination irregularities, including the NEET-UG paper leak.The panel is headed by Nilekani. Its members include former ISRO chairman S Somanath, former Intelligence Bureau director Tapan Deka, IIT Madras director V Kamakoti, former education secretary Anita Karwal and logistics expert Amrit Lal Meena.The panel was constituted in July to recommend reforms in the examination system following the controversy surrounding NEET-UG.
Article Summary: Several states suggest multiple NEET-UG attempts in a year and weightage to Class 12 scores as part of examination reforms. The proposals have been made to a high-powered task force led by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani. The suggestions aim to reduce students' dependence on a single high-stakes entrance test.

SRINAGAR: Jammu & Kashmir govt is set to reserve 25% of seats in the entry-level class in private unaided schools for children from economically weaker sections (EWS) and disadvantaged groups, in accordance with Section 12(1)(c) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.Education minister Shamim Firdous made this announcement during a meeting with representatives of private school associations, parents’ associations, and members of civil society in Srinagar Tuesday.“The rules governing the implementation of RTE Section 12(1)(c) are in the final stage and a notification will be issued shortly... The initiative is aimed at promoting inclusive education, ensuring equitable access to quality schooling and extending greater educational opportunities to children from underprivileged backgrounds,” she added.The govt will reimburse such schools for admissible expenditure incurred on implementing the scheme.The minister said that students must not be burdened with unnecessary additional or supplementary books, reiterating that the principles of NEP 2020 call for a balanced, flexible and child-centred approach to learning.“Where supplementary educational resources are considered necessary, schools may facilitate access through libraries, book banks, e-books and other digital learning resources rather than compelling parents to buy multiple additional books,” she added.
Article Summary: Jammu & Kashmir govt is set to reserve 25% of seats in the entry-level class in private unaided schools for children from economically weaker sections (EWS) and disadvantaged groups. NEW DELHI: Greater focus should be on citizen experience, rather than on number of schemes and programmes implemented, said PM's principal secretary PK Mishra Tuesday, as he called for seamless coordination across govt departments. Article Title: 'Heavens will not fall': SC on ED plea challenging Azam Khan's interim bail
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to stay the Allahabad high court order granting interim bail to Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan in a money laundering case. The court observed that "heavens will not fall" if the order was allowed to stand.However, a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant agreed to hear the Enforcement Directorate 's appeal on Thursday.The ED had approached the Supreme Court challenging the high court's decision, arguing that the interim bail order was passed in haste and without giving the agency adequate opportunity to present its case.When the ED sought a status quo on the high court order, a bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to intervene immediately. "Let him be on interim bail. Heavens will not fall if we do not stay the HC order," the bench said.Appearing for the ED, Additional Solicitor General SV Raju submitted that the high court had effectively decided the matter finally through an interim order. He also argued that the agency was not allowed to file its complete counter-affidavit and that its request for a trial court report on the service of arrest papers to Khan was not considered.The CJI directed that the matter be listed for hearing on Thursday.The Allahabad High Court had granted interim bail to the 78-year-old SP leader on Tuesday in the money laundering case, observing that the ED had failed to furnish written grounds of arrest when taking him into custody on October 31.The high court had also described the proceedings as "motivated" and "mala fide", pointing out that Khan was arrested moments after being released from jail in another case. It had granted the ED a week to file its counter-affidavit.Khan, who is lodged at Dasna jail in Ghaziabad, was arrested in connection with a money laundering probe linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and the construction of the Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur.His interim bail came on a day when the Supreme Court also dismissed the Uttar Pradesh government's appeal against the suspension of his conviction in the fake birth certificate case, while granting similar relief to his wife, Tazeen Fatma, and son, Abdullah Azam Khan.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant agreed to hear Enforcement Directorate's appeal on Thursday. The ED had approached the Supreme Court challenging the high court's decision. The court observed that "heavens will not fall" if the order was allowed to stand.

Article Title: Unvaccinated yellow fever-risk travellers may face six-day quarantine; new airport rules propose changes
Article Text:
India has unveiled draft regulations enhancing quarantine protocols for travelers from yellow fever-affected nations. (Pic Credit: AI Generated)

NEW DELHI: Travellers arriving in India from countries like Nigeria, Kenya, and Venezuela affected by yellow fever without a valid vaccination certificate could face quarantine for up to six days, with the cost to be borne by them, while airlines will have to pay for their transportation to designated facilities. This is among the key changes proposed in the draft Indian Aircraft (Public Health) Rules, 2026, which seek to replace the 1954 regulations.Under the existing rules, unvaccinated travellers could be isolated for up to nine days from the last possible exposure. The new draft proposes a maximum six-day quarantine counted from the date of departure from the yellow fever-affected country. Travellers unwilling to undergo quarantine can be denied entry and sent back without leaving the airport transit area.The proposed rules also seek to widen airport health oversight beyond specific infectious diseases to cover pandemics, public-health emergencies and chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear and explosive hazards.Airport food outlets and flight kitchens will have to be licensed under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Drinking water quality will have to be tested at source, with regular reports submitted to Airport Health Officers, who can order unsafe food to be discarded and close establishments or water sources found unsafe.The 1954 rules required aircraft disinsection in specific situations, including flights arriving from areas affected by mosquito-borne diseases or yellow fever. The 2026 draft proposes making disinsection mandatory for all arriving aircraft, while also requiring airport premises and surrounding areas extending at least 400 metres beyond the airport perimeter to be kept free of mosquitoes, rats and other disease-carrying vectors.Airlines will face more detailed reporting obligations, including submission of passenger manifests and information on illness or deaths on board. Airport Health Officers can seek passenger locator forms, contact details, destinations, travel itineraries and seat numbers, even outside a public-health emergency.The draft also introduces a defined penalty schedule and a two-stage appeal mechanism against orders passed by Airport Health Officers. It specifies monetary penalties for different violations, while appeals can be filed within 30 days and should, as far as possible, be disposed of within 60 days.The health ministry has invited comments from government departments, airport operators, airlines and other stakeholders within 30 days of its November 16 memorandum. The draft will be forwarded to the Ministry of Civil Aviation for further action after the suggestions are examined.
Article Summary: India has unveiled draft regulations enhancing quarantine protocols for travelers from yellow fever-affected nations. Unvaccinated travellers could be isolated for up to nine days from the last possible exposure. Travellers unwilling to undergo quarantine can be denied entry and sent back without leaving the airport transit area.

Article Title: NMC asks medical colleges to vet draft rules seeking tighter checks on animal experiments
Article Text:
The National Medical Commission has introduced new draft rules to enhance the ethical treatment of laboratory animals in research.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The use of laboratory animals in medical research could face tighter restrictions, with draft rules requiring researchers to explore alternatives to live animals wherever scientifically possible, minimise their numbers and reduce pain and suffering. The proposals also seek to prohibit experiments involving severe suffering that is likely to be prolonged and cannot be alleviated.In a public notice issued on Monday, the National Medical Commission (NMC) asked Deans, Principals and Heads of medical colleges and institutions to submit their comments, objections and suggestions to the Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals (CCSEA) within 30 days. The draft rules were notified on September 30 and published in the Gazette of India on October 6.The rules place the principles of replacement, reduction and refinement at the centre of animal research. They classify experiments as non-recovery, mild, moderate and severe, and prohibit those likely to cause prolonged, severe suffering that cannot be alleviated.Veterinary supervision would be mandatory for all experiments, with every establishment involved in animal research or breeding required to appoint a veterinarian.Each establishment would also have to set up a nine-member Institutional Animal Ethics Committee, with a three-year tenure, to oversee experiments. The committee would include scientists, a biologist, a veterinarian and four CCSEA nominees, and meet at least twice a year.The draft also seeks to avoid death as an experimental endpoint wherever possible, requiring researchers to use early humane endpoints. Where death is unavoidable, the number of animals affected and the duration and intensity of suffering must be minimised. Establishments would have to maintain records of euthanasia, including the method, dosage and reason.The use of stray and feral domestic animals would be restricted, with exceptions allowed only when their use is scientifically justified. Experiments on non-human primates would be permitted only for narrowly defined research purposes where no other species can serve the objective.All establishments conducting animal experiments or breeding, housing and trading laboratory animals would require CCSEA registration and face inspections at least twice a year. Violations could invite a 15-day notice to rectify deficiencies, followed by suspension or cancellation for repeated non-compliance. Immediate action would be allowed in cases of imminent risk to animal welfare.
Article Summary: The National Medical Commission has introduced new draft rules to enhance the ethical treatment of laboratory animals in research. The rules place the principles of replacement, reduction and refinement at the centre of animal research. Experiments on non-human primates would be permitted only for narrowly defined research purposes where no other species can serve the objective.

Article Title: India ranks 10th in Climate Risk Index, with 78,000 deaths and $170 billion in losses from 436 extreme weather events over 1996–2025
Article Text:
People walk past damaged homes near the shore at Uppada, in Kakinada, India, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026 after Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast.

Climate Risk Index 2027

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: More than 9,00,000 people lost their lives worldwide due to weather extremes, resulting in direct economic losses totalling more than $4.7 trillion in the past 30 years (1996-2025), with India figuring as the 10th most affected country by recording 78,000 deaths and losing $170 billion due to 436 extreme events during the period, shows a Climate Risk Index (CRI) 2027 report by a Germany-based environment and development organisation released on Tuesday.In annual terms, the report, released on the sidelines of the ongoing UN climate conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye, put the number of extreme weather events in 2025 at 367 — it means the world averaged one disaster every single day last year.The events in 2025 caused nearly 35,000 fatalities, affected more than 100 million people and caused direct economic losses exceeding $158 billion worldwise. The year-wise index put India at 12th position, with the CRI annual ranking flagging Jamaica, Sri Lanka and Spain as the first three most affected countries, followed by Thailand, the Philippines, Pakistan, Indonesia, Bolivia, Mozambique and Vietnam in the top 10.In the previous year’s report, India was placed at ninth position on the long-term (1995-2024) index and at 15th rank in the year-wise index of 2024. As per the CRI, a lower rank means less risk. In the long term, China figures at 11th position in both 1995-2024 and 1996-2025 CRIs.The analysis shows that heat waves were by far the deadliest extreme weather events in 2025 that caused nearly 70% of all reported disaster fatalities (more than 24,000 deaths).Over the past 30 years, heatwaves have accounted for the largest share of reported fatalities (40%).On the other hand, storms are by far the costliest hazard over the three-decade period, accounting for 58% of economic losses in 1996–2025. In 2025, storms also caused the greatest economic losses (41% of all such losses, nearly $65 billion in total).“Among the ten countries most affected in the past 30 years, the Bahamas is the only one that is per definition a high income country. At the top of the list are nine countries that have been particularly hard-hit by devastating tropical cyclones—often repeatedly, with subsequent storms destroying structures that had already been rebuilt,” said Laura Schäfer, one of the authors of the CRI report, released by Germanwatch.The CRI shows that the affected countries had unequal climate impacts. Over the 30-year period, the results confirm that lower-income countries that have contributed the least to climate change bear its heaviest costs.In 1996–2025, nine of the 10 most affected countries were from the lower- and upper-middle-income groups, with the Bahamas as the only high-income country.CRI analyses the number of deaths, people affected, and economic damage caused by extreme weather events – both in absolute terms and in relation to population size and gross domestic product. It is compiled based on data from the International Disaster Database on extreme weather events and socio-economic data from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank.
Article Summary: More than 9,00,000 people lost their lives worldwide due to weather extremes, resulting in direct economic losses totalling more than $4.7 trillion in the past 30 years. India figuring as the 10th most affected country by recording 78,000 deaths and losing $170 billion due to 436 extreme events during the period.

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar filed an affidavit in Supreme Court on Tuesday saying permission to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar on Oct 10 was denied given Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) non-compliance with past undertakings for peaceful protest and intelligence inputs pointing towards a possible “dangerous situation” causing a serious public order problem.“A major public order situation was averted (on Oct 10) by timely, proportionate and lawful measures taken by Delhi Police,” the commissioner said, adding, “Keeping this scenario in mind, certain preventive steps were required to be taken. One such step was to prevent anyone to become part of an unlawful assembly and to participate in commission of cognisable offences as a consequence of assembling at Jantar Mantar. ” In his affidavit, Kumar said all protesters, including politicians, who were removed from Jantar Mantar on Oct 10 were neither detained nor arrested but kept in makeshift centres or in the SHO’s room in police stations and were provided with refreshments.Also Read| SC to hear INDIA bloc's poser plea on CEC on Dec 9 Kumar said SC must take a holistic view of the matter, its sensitivity and the preventive measures taken by police. “No police administration can permit breach of public order in the national capital, particularly when a call is given by an organisation with a recent history of mob violence, destruction of public and private property, and incidents resulting in injuries to several individuals and the subsequent protests (by Congress) on Oct 6, 7, 8,” he said.“Certain regulatory measures were introduced for regulating 57 Metro stations on Oct 9 but the same was reviewed pursuant to the SC order and only 45 of 303 Metro stations were regulated,” he added.Dealing with law and order was a highly sensitive aspect of policing, requiring a delicate balance between the right to protest of some on the one hand, and the rights of other citizens to lead their normal and peaceful life, he said.The potential danger to life and property of citizens and public property also needed to be kept in mind, he added.Kumar said CJP was given permission to hold a peaceful protest for a day on June 20 and it had given an undertaking that the number of protesters would be around 1,000. Contrary to the undertaking and in violation of the permission, CJP erected temporary structures at Jantar Mantar and, in violation of prohibitory orders, organised a march to Parliament on July 20, he added.
Article Summary: Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar filed an affidavit in Supreme Court on Tuesday. He said permission to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar on Oct 10 was denied given Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) non-compliance with past undertakings for peaceful protest.

New Delhi: A man in Chhattisgarh lost his youth in jail for a crime he did not commit - first seven years in legal detention when he was being tried in a murder case, but his problem did not end with his acquittal as he had to suffer a further seven years of incarceration because the HC order was not conveyed to him and the jail authorities, reports Amitanand Choudhary. Article Title: Must remain politically neutral but learn from extraordinary leaders: Cabinet secy to babus
Article Text:
Cabinet secretary TV Somnathan (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Civil servants have a constitutional duty to remain politically neutral, but they should learn administrative skills of extraordinary leaders, cabinet secretary T V Somanathan said on Wednesday, drawing on his experience of working with PM Narendra Modi and former Tamil Nadu CM M Karunanidhi.Addressing a leadership workshop for civil servants, Somanathan said elected heads of govt combine political and administrative leadership, and while bureaucrats must stay away from politics, they should learn from the latter aspect of their leadership.“While staying away from the political aspect, we can and should learn from the administrative skills of extraordinary leaders and that is the purpose of this workshop,” he said.Somanathan, who served as secretary to CM under Karunanidhi for around four years and worked in PMO for two-and-a-half years as joint secretary and additional secretary, said the longevity of the two leaders as heads of govt reflected extraordinary leadership skills. Karunanidhi held office for over 19 years, while Modi has completed 25 years as head of govt.Sharing lessons on leadership and governance, he said the questions senior officers raise during review meetings shape the priorities of officials down the administrative chain.If reviews focus only on expenditure, districts will concentrate on spending, but asking how many beneficiaries have actually received the intended benefits would shift attention towards outcomes.The Cabinet Secretary also emphasised the importance of listening directly to citizens rather than relying entirely on information filtered through several layers of administration. “Every senior officer needs a few sources of information that have not been summarised by anyone,” he said, citing field visits, reading individual grievances and meeting visitors as ways to understand problems that may not figure in official reports.On decision-making, Somanathan said files should not be viewed as obstacles, as recording reasons, facts and options considered gives decisions legitimacy and helps them withstand scrutiny. “A sense of mission in the civil service must therefore work hand in hand with a sense of propriety and due process,” he said. Officers should not avoid taking decisions when file notings and advice differ, but must record cogent reasons before proceeding, even if it means overruling objections.Somanathan also urged senior officials to delegate authority and stand by juniors who take decisions in good faith. “Officers will use the authority they already have only when they are confident that their seniors will not leave them to face the consequences alone when something goes wrong,” he said.On the need for course correction, he said well-reasoned changes in implementation should be seen as evidence of a programme learning from experience, rather than a deviation. The cabinet secretary also said leadership should also be judged by whether work continues effectively after an officer is transferred, stressing the importance of proper handover notes and institutional continuity.Somanathan urged officers to take decisions in public interest, record their reasons clearly and ensure that successors and reviewing authorities understand the rationale behind them.
Article Summary: Civil servants have a constitutional duty to remain politically neutral. But they should learn administrative skills of extraordinary leaders, cabinet secretary says. T V Somanathan draws on his experience of working with PM Narendra Modi and former Tamil Nadu CM M Karunanidhi.

NEW DELHI: Congress' former ally and Raijor Dal MLA Akhil Gogoi on Tuesday accused the grand old party and Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi of weakening the Cockroach Janata Dal (CJP) agitation through "parallel protests".In a letter sent to Rahul, Gogoi described the CJP agitation as the "single most powerful and effective people's movement capable of shaking this dictatorship" since 2014. Let me state this clearly from decades of grassroots struggle: if there is no independent people’s movement, there is no chance of changing this communal-fascist government,” the letter read.Gogoi also said that Congress had weakened the genuine mass revolt by dividing the streets and competing with the movement, claiming that the move gave the government room to contain it.“Since 2014, the CJP agitation has been the single most powerful and effective people’s movement capable of shaking this dictatorship. Within five months, it awakened the youth where traditional opposition politics had failed for twelve years. Yet, instead of standing solidly behind this organic uprising, the Indian National Congress launched parallel protests. By dividing the streets and competing with a genuine mass revolt, your party weakened the CJP movement, gave the ruling regime room to contain it, and squandered the nation’s best opportunity for a decisive fight,” he wrote.“You cannot defeat a fascist regime through party control or press-conference politics. Real political change only happens through an honest, independent people’s movement backed unconditionally by the opposition,” he added.Warning of the opposition’s electoral prospects in 2029, Gogoi wrote, “Otherwise, even if you disagree with me, I must tell you plainly that the opposition will not be able to overthrow this people’s enemy government in 2029.”This was the third letter Gogoi had written to Rahul Gandhi after receiving no response to his earlier letters dated October 29 and November 12.Gogoi also urged the Congress leader to respond to his concerns and address what he described as a strategic error by Congress.“I urge you to break your silence, confront this grave strategic error, and reply to me at the earliest,” he wrote.Gogoi had also written to political activist Yogendra Yadav regarding the issue, amid differences over the breakdown of his party’s alliance with Congress in Assam.Congress snapped ties with Raijor Dal in September, accusing the regional party of violating coalition ethics and undermining the alliance.The split followed disagreements over seat-sharing, with Akhil Gogoi claiming that Raijor Dal had sought 13 seats but Congress was willing to offer only four.Gogoi also accused Congress of arrogance, alleging that Gaurav Gogoi had unilaterally finalised the party's candidates' list without consulting its alliance partners.

Article Title: Quad steps up Indo-Pacific push with new maritime, AI initiatives; warns against economic coercion

NEW DELHI: The Quad on Tuesday announced a series of new initiatives to deepen cooperation on maritime security, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and business ties. They also raised concerns over economic coercion and unilateral attempts to change the regional status quo.At the Quad Leaders’ Summit in Manila, leaders of India, the United States, Australia and Japan revealed plans for a Quad Business Leaders' Forum, enhanced cybersecurity cooperation and a new maritime surveillance initiative. They also reaffirmed their commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific, with an emphasis on protecting vital supply chains and ensuring safe maritime routes.In a joint statement issued after the meeting, US president Donald Trump, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese and Japanese prime minister Takaichi Sanae said the grouping remained committed to peace, stability and prosperity in the region.“We strongly oppose any destabilising or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability,” the leaders said.They also expressed “grave concerns” over economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions, and pledged to work together to secure critical supply chains, protect freedom of navigation and overflight, and expand the use of trusted technologies.A key announcement was the launch of the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration, aimed at improving information-sharing and maritime domain awareness across the region.The leaders said Quad countries' P-8 and P-3C maritime patrol aircraft were scheduled to take part in a joint maritime exercise in 2027. It would be the first such exercise involving the aircraft in a Quad context, according to the statement.The initiative is intended to strengthen the grouping's ability to monitor maritime activity and contribute to safer sea routes across the Indo-Pacific.The leaders also committed to ensuring open, safe and resilient maritime transit corridors, underlining the importance of freedom of navigation and overflight.The Quad announced the inaugural Quad Business Leaders' Forum, scheduled to be held in early 2027. It will bring together business leaders, government officials and policy experts from the four countries to strengthen private-sector ties and encourage commercial deals and partnerships across the Indo-Pacific.The leaders also reaffirmed their support for the AI Accelerator, announced by their foreign ministers in Atlanta. The initiative is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to improve access to trusted AI, its deployment and technical assistance across the region.The joint statement also highlighted progress under the Quad Partnership for Cable Connectivity and Resilience, which aims to expand access to secure communications infrastructure.Australia will expand its contribution to the partnership to include electricity cables, with the stated aim of strengthening regional energy security and connectivity. The leaders also welcomed upcoming undersea cable projects in the Indian Ocean.The four countries announced enhanced Quad Cybersecurity Cooperation, citing a rapid increase in the number and scale of cyber incidents across the region. The initiative is intended to strengthen cooperation towards an open and secure cyberspace.The leaders also unequivocally condemned terrorism and violent extremism in all forms, including cross-border terrorism, and committed to strengthening the grouping's existing counterterrorism cooperation.Reaffirming their support for Asean centrality and unity, the leaders said they would continue working with regional partners to address shared challenges and deliver tangible benefits across the Indo-Pacific.The Manila summit comes nearly a decade after the Quad was revived in 2017. The joint statement also marked the 10th anniversary of the vision of a Free and Open Indo-Pacific, first articulated by former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe in 2016.
Article Summary: Leaders of India, the United States, Australia and Japan revealed plans for a Quad Business Leaders' Forum, enhanced cybersecurity cooperation and a new maritime surveillance initiative. Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Donald Trump is pushing ahead with restrictions on Chinese equipment used inside US AI data centres despite objections from Amazon, Google and Meta; tech firms say replacing the components could take
Article Text:
Before the Trump-Xi summit, Beijing urges Washington to ease export bans on critical AI chips.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your primary concern regarding US-China tech relations? National Security Economic Impact Innovation Stifling 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Beneath the sleek server racks powering the modern artificial intelligence boom lies an intricate web of fiber-optic cables, microchips, and cross-border dependencies that neither Washington nor Beijing can easily untangle. Even as diplomatic backchannels open ahead of a potential summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping , the technological cold war between the world’s two largest economies is entering a high-stakes standoff over the physical building blocks of AI.Washington targets data center hardwareAccording to Reuters, the Trump administration is pressing forward with plans to block US imports of new Chinese optical transceivers, the vital components that transmit data at light speed across fiber-optic cables inside AI data centers. Despite fierce resistance from Silicon Valley’s biggest hyperscalers—including Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, CoreWeave, and Cisco—federal regulators at the Federal Communications Commission are advancing the restriction over national security fears that Beijing could exploit the hardware to harvest sensitive data, implant malware, or cripple critical computing infrastructure, adds the online report.During a previously undisclosed meeting with White House officials earlier this year, executives from these tech giants warned that replacing Chinese-made transceivers could take up to a decade, Reuters reported. Market realities explain why: Chinese suppliers such as Eoptolink and Zhongji Innolight control roughly two-thirds of global optical transceiver production, while American alternatives like Coherent and Lumentum currently lack the manufacturing scale to fill the void. Following news of the administration’s resolve, shares of Coherent and Lumentum climbed, even as tech leaders cautioned that Beijing could retaliate by halting exports of indium phosphide, a critical mineral required to manufacture domestic transceivers.Beijing presses for chip reliefWhile Washington tightens the screws on networking hardware, Beijing is lobbying aggressively to loosen existing American chokeholds on semiconductor technology. According to WION, Chinese trade negotiators have urged US counterparts to relax export bans on high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips ahead of the anticipated Trump-Xi summit. HBM chips are needed to stack memory and logic components for data-heavy AI models, but Biden administration restrictions in 2024 have severely limited Chinese champions like Huawei and SMIC.Chinese officials argue that the curbs unfairly obstruct their legitimate commercial access to global supply chains, WION noted. However, national security hawks and industry analysts in Washington warn that easing HBM restrictions would hand Huawei and SMIC a lifeline, enabling them to scale domestic AI chip production and erode the market dominance of American firms like Nvidia.Smuggling scandal fuels Hawkish momentumAlthough President Trump has adopted a relatively measured tone toward Beijing during his second term amid Chinese export controls on vital rare-earth minerals, the FCC has aggressively barred new Chinese drones, routers, robots, and power inverters over the past year, Reuters reported.Momentum for the optical transceiver crackdown has been further supercharged by political fallout surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy, according to Reuters. The controversy has intensified scrutiny over enforcement gaps at the Commerce Department, particularly regarding cases in which advanced Nvidia chips were smuggled into China or where non-AI gaming processors were repurposed for artificial intelligence workloads, WION reported.Lawmakers including Representative John Moolenaar have demanded stricter oversight to close these loopholes.While a White House official maintained to Reuters that recent FCC restrictions have spurred billions of dollars in domestic manufacturing investments, the Chinese Embassy in Washington condemned the administration for overstretching national security concepts and vowed to defend Chinese corporate interests. Caught between geopolitical security mandates and decade-long supply chain realities, America’s AI giants now face a turbulent transition.Images Courtesy: istock and Instagram
Article Summary: Beijing is lobbying aggressively to loosen existing American chokeholds on semiconductor technology. China has urged US counterparts to relax export bans on high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips ahead of the anticipated Trump-Xi summit. Washington is pressing forward with plans to block US imports of new Chinese optical transceivers.

PUNE: The Pune District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed an interior designer to pay over Rs 6.14 lakh, along with interest, to a woman for allegedly providing substandard interior work and defective furniture at her Balewadi flat.The commission partially allowed a complaint filed by Lopamudra Chakraborty against Dwipesh Barua, founder and proprietor of creArt – House of Interiors. The two entered into a residential interior design services agreement on April 28, 2019, with the work scheduled to be completed within 75 days, by July 10, 2019.The original estimated cost was Rs 9.83 lakh, but the designer collected Rs 11.21 lakh, citing an increase in raw material prices, the complaint stated.Chakraborty alleged that the designer used inferior-quality materials, delayed the work beyond the agreed deadline and left several defects unaddressed.
